proposed_widenings.name: save_gated_ongoing_effect
proposed_widenings.justification: Ray of Enfeeblement opens with a CON save whose two branches have mechanically distinct duration semantics: success → fleeting effect expiring at start of caster's next turn; failure → full concentration-duration ongoing effects. No existing family supports 'initial save gate determines whether/which ongoing effects activate'. activation family forces onFail/onSuccess into Effect (damage|none only). ongoing_effect family has no initial save gate. A new family — or a structural extension of activation that allows 'on-fail: activate ongoing operation for spell duration' — is required.
proposed_widenings.evidence: On a failed save, the target has Disadvantage on Strength-based D20 Tests for the duration. During that time, it also subtracts 1d8 from all its damage rolls. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell on a success.

proposed_widenings.name: repeat_save_expiry
proposed_widenings.justification: The spell includes a repeat-save mechanic: target saves at end of each of its turns; success ends the spell. The v4 atom repeat_save exists but has no surface expression inside any existing SpellMechanics family. The lifetime of the ongoing effect is governed by this iterative save, not by fixed time or concentration-break alone.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell on a success.

proposed_widenings.name: Effect: modify_roll_advantage
proposed_widenings.justification: The success branch of the initial save imposes disadvantage on the target's next attack roll. Effect = DamageEffect | NoneEffect; there is no modify_roll_advantage variant for spell phase effects. The atom exists in v4 (MasteryEffect) but is not reachable from ActivationPhase.onSuccess/onFail.
proposed_widenings.evidence: On a successful save, the target has Disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes until the start of your next turn.

proposed_widenings.name: OngoingOperation or Effect: modify_damage_roll (subtract from damage rolls)
proposed_widenings.justification: The failure branch applies '-1d8 from all damage rolls'. RollKind covers attack_roll and saving_throw; damage rolls are not in scope. RollModifierOperation.on is ReadonlyArray<RollKind> and cannot target damage rolls. A new OngoingOperation kind (e.g. modify_damage_output) or a new RollKind value 'damage_roll' is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: it also subtracts 1d8 from all its damage rolls

proposed_widenings.name: RollKind: ability_check
proposed_widenings.justification: The failure effect applies disadvantage on 'Strength-based D20 Tests', which in SRD 5.2.1 encompasses STR attack rolls, STR saving throws, AND STR ability checks. Current RollKind = 'attack_roll' | 'saving_throw' — ability checks are absent. A RollKind of 'ability_check' (or a filter-by-ability variant) is needed to correctly scope this effect.
proposed_widenings.evidence: the target has Disadvantage on Strength-based D20 Tests for the duration

notes: The spell's structure is fundamentally a save-gated ongoing effect with two asymmetric outcomes (fleeting effect on success, persistent multi-effect concentration on failure) plus a turn-end repeat-save expiry. This combination does not fit activation (Effect union too narrow, no ongoing persistence from phase results) or ongoing_effect (no initial save gate). The structural gap drives the classification to structural_widening rather than surface_widening: even adding the missing Effect variants would not provide the save-gate → ongoing-effect activation path or the repeat_save lifecycle. All five widenings are necessary to encode this spell honestly.
